title: Malformed Excel and PowerPoint packages can become valid-looking empty or mis-mapped models

evidence.quote: const partPath = target ? normalizePartPath(target) : `xl/worksheets/sheet${sheets.length + 1}.xml`; ... if (!partXml) continue;
const worksheet = findChild(root, 'worksheet'); const sheetData = findChild(childrenOf(worksheet ?? ({} as XNode)), 'sheetData');
parse the underlying OOXML (.docx/.xlsx/.pptx are ZIP archives of XML)

reasoning: The Excel and PowerPoint adapters do not fail when required OOXML relationships, parts, or roots are missing. They fall back to positional part names, skip missing referenced parts, or return empty sheet/slide content. A corrupt or malformed Office file can therefore be snapshotted as if whole sheets, slides, or shapes were deleted, or as if a sheet/slide id pointed at the wrong part, which undermines trustworthy diffs and can corrupt DocGit history.
recommendation: Require every workbook sheet and presentation slide relationship to resolve to an existing part, validate required XML roots before parsing children, and throw a descriptive parse error on malformed packages. Only keep any positional fallback behind an explicit, tested compatibility path that cannot silently mislabel content.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked tests only cover happy-path relationships and missing top-level workbook/presentation files; they do not cover unresolved r:id values, missing referenced sheet/slide parts, malformed worksheet XML, or malformed presentation XML.
suggestedRegressionTest: Create .xlsx and .pptx fixtures whose workbook/presentation lists an r:id that is absent from the rels file, and fixtures whose rel target points to a missing part; assert parseXlsx/parsePptx throw instead of returning a model with skipped or fallback content. Add malformed worksheet and presentation-root cases as well.
minimumFixScope: Tighten relationship resolution and required-node validation in packages/core/src/adapters/excel/parse.ts and packages/core/src/adapters/powerpoint/parse.ts, with regression tests in excel.test.ts and powerpoint.test.ts.
